answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so the binding constraint is not increasing delivery risk. Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms is blocked this cycle; defer_decision and a dual-source add leave a supply gap we cannot cover with one action. memory_c1 is the load-bearing stability case for staying; memory_c2 (successful low-cost cutover) will be checked before any switch is considered, because a 14-day primary flip at this utilization would put downstream output at risk even if last year's onboarding was clean. Until those records are confirmed, renew the incumbent to keep continuity; cost-mandate pressure is real but a stockout would dominate TCO.
